clue.text: Pure terror, no mistake, during hunt

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the span of the other

parts.note: to hunt is to chase

indicators.note: no says the following word is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: a mistake is an error

explanation.surface: A frightened quarry flees in pure terror, with no slip allowed during the hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no mistake' strips ERROR from TERROR, leaving T, which goes 'during' CHASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone pure in the moral sense is virtuous and abstinent.

clue.text: Person creating buzz over article

indicators.note: in a down entry over says the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a buzz is a hum
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone causing a stir about a piece in the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buzz' suggests excitement, but it is the sound HUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a human being is an individual.

clue.text: Chatted in favour of being romantically attached?

parts.note: chatted is the past of speak, spoken being its past participle
for means in favour of, as in voting for

explanation.surface: Someone talked in support of being in a relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link; the question mark signals the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a person already claimed by a partner is not available to court.

clue.text: Applaud European vote on quota raised

parts.note: X is the mark made on a ballot paper

indicators.note: raised in a down entry means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a lot is a share or quota

explanation.surface: An EU politician welcomes a vote on raising a quota.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to praise highly is to cheer or commend.

clue.text: Bound to protect soldiers in ranks

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: bound means tied up
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Duty requires guarding troops lined up in formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like the verb 'obliged'; it is TIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something arranged in ranks or rows one above another is layered.

clue.text: Sour end to cooked filet mignon

indicators.note: cooked means doctored or tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A disappointing finish to a steak dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: small round steaks cut from the beef tenderloin.

clue.text: Spirit stifled by cabinet hostility

indicators.note: stifled by means smothered inside, so the letters lie within these words

explanation.surface: Team spirit is crushed by hostility within the cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the characteristic spirit or values of a group or culture.

clue.text: Heroic hospital department about to become focus of disturbance

parts.note: epic means heroic
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A dramatic hospital unit is about to become the centre of attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the point above an earthquake's origin, the centre of the shaking.

clue.text: Co-ordinates of signal readjusted

indicators.note: readjusted means set again differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Map co-ordinates from a signal have been corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Co-ordinates' looks like a noun; it is the verb, puts in line.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to co-ordinate is to bring into line or arrange together.

clue.text: Watch, getting shilling admission

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for shilling, an old British coin
admission is entry

explanation.surface: A watch bought for the price of a shilling entrance fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a timepiece; it is a guard on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a guard keeping watch, a lookout.

clue.text: Branch office's first dance

parts.note: a branch of a tree is a limb

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word office

explanation.surface: A branch office holds its first staff dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Caribbean dance where performers bend backwards under a lowered bar.

clue.text: Contact business that puts a limit on pitch

definitions.text: that puts a limit on pitch

parts.note: contact means touch
a line is a line of business, a trade

explanation.surface: A firm that makes contact, then something that sets a limit on a sales pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' is a sports field, not a sales pitch or musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the boundary marking along each side of a football or rugby field.

clue.text: Well-mannered chap left beyond the outskirts of Eastbourne

indicators.note: beyond says the next piece comes after what precedes it

parts.note: a chap is a gent

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its outside letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A polite gentleman has moved out past the edge of the seaside town of Eastbourne.
explanation.walkthrough: Eastbourne is a resort on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: refined, polite and respectable in manner.

clue.text: Emerging name with a fragrance

parts.note: a fragrance is a scent

explanation.surface: A new perfume brand is being launched with a name and a fragrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: just coming into existence and beginning to develop.

clue.text: Composure required if dragon's to be disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed letters are knocked out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: You would need nerves of steel if you were going to disturb a sleeping dragon.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed French idiom for coolness and calm under pressure.

clue.text: Africans shifting earnings across Italy

indicators.note: across means spanning, so one piece stretches around the other
shifting means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Workers moving their earnings across Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: people from a West African nation.

clue.text: Downtrodden and in a hurry to underpin work

indicators.note: to underpin is to support from beneath, so in a down entry this piece sits under the other

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
pressed for time means in a hurry

explanation.surface: Exhausted workers rushed to shore up their task.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: kept down by cruel or unjust treatment.

clue.text: Races in to purchase something to relieve hunger

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to purchase is to buy
TT is the Tourist Trophy, the Isle of Man motorcycle races

explanation.surface: Someone dashes in to buy a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: A BUTTY is British slang for a sandwich, such as a bacon butty.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a sandwich is a quick bite eaten to ease an empty stomach.

clue.text: Cover eyes, having difficulty accommodating student congregation

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a bind is a difficulty or nuisance
L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car
a fold is a flock, a church congregation

explanation.surface: A student struggling to fit in with a church community covers their eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a band tied over the face to stop someone seeing, or the act of tying it.

clue.text: Row about end of breeding animal in zoo

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a row of seats is a tier

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word breeding

explanation.surface: An argument over a zoo's breeding programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a TIER of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a big striped cat commonly kept in zoos.

clue.text: Develop a liking for scene with couple on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than read, so the words are matched by their sound

parts.note: a scene is a take in filming, and a couple is two: together a second take

explanation.surface: Getting fond of a romantic scene featuring a pair, broadcast on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to come to like or warm to someone or something.

clue.text: Bug advanced carrying one likely to cause disease

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the pair of pieces encloses the other

parts.note: a bug is a pest
advanced money is lent
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An advanced bug is carrying a germ likely to make people ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: harmful or infectious, like a plague.

clue.text: After time, quietens kids

indicators.note: After places the second piece behind the first

parts.note: eases means calms or quietens

explanation.surface: After a while, the parent calms the children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kids' looks like a noun for children; it is the verb, pulls someone's leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to kid someone is to rib or make fun of them.

clue.text: Drunken rake should welcome a fine form of entertainment

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other
drunken suggests reeling about, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: OK means fine

explanation.surface: A drunken rogue ought to be greeted with a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like a penalty to welcome the rake with; it is the word of approval, OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pub pastime of singing along to recorded backing tracks.

clue.text: Write up area report to include performance on stage

indicators.note: Write up says the hidden letters are read backwards
to include means to contain, so the letters lie within these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A journalist's write-up of a local report featuring a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'to include' in the definition, but it is the indicator signalling that the letters sit inside 'area report'; the definition is 'performance on stage'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sung dramatic work performed in a theatre.

clue.text: Agitated air following rejection of cheese and wine

indicators.note: following says this piece comes after the one before
a rejection throws something back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A flustered diner turns down cheese and wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheese and wine' reads as a party, but only 'wine' is the definition; the cheese is Dutch Edam.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fortified dessert wine from the Portuguese island of the same name.

clue.text: Spoilt young woman married the first man

parts.note: Adam was the first man in Genesis

explanation.surface: A pampered girl wed the very first man.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal sense: a bossy, precocious girl is called a little madam.

clue.text: Images of prisoner held by discontented interrogators

indicators.note: held by means gripped inside, so one piece goes within the other
discontented means emptied of contents, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: Pictures of a captive detained by unhappy questioners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' looks like unhappy; it strips INTERROGATORS to its ends, IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: icons are pictures, especially religious ones or on-screen symbols.

clue.text: Crooked advertiser — I held out and negotiated

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
held out means kept away, so this letter is removed from the word

explanation.surface: A dishonest advertiser holds out in a bargaining session before agreeing terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held out' takes I from ADVERTISER, leaving ADVERTSER for 'Crooked' to rearrange. 'negotiated' means got across, as in negotiating an obstacle, not bargained.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to negotiate a hazard is to cross or pass over it successfully.

clue.text: Gas area on the west of Oregon

indicators.note: on says the next piece is added after the one before
in an across entry the west of a word is its leftmost, first letter

parts.note: an area is a zone

explanation.surface: A region of the American Northwest, west of Oregon, is affected by gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a form of oxygen gas with three atoms per molecule.

clue.text: Single line found in smooth traffic-free area of street

parts.note: I, the Roman one, means single

indicators.note: found in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to sand wood is to smooth it

explanation.surface: A single lane marking found on a smooth pedestrian zone.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a traffic refuge, the raised spot mid-road where pedestrians can wait.

clue.text: Two ways to be humble

parts.note: a mode is a way of doing something
ST, short for street, is the second way: the clue's 'Two ways' supplies two words for way

explanation.surface: A homily offering two paths to humility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two ways' gives two different words for way: MODE (a manner) and ST (a street).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unassuming and not boastful.
